newsitem.title: INDIA: ICICI says loss provision not to hit net.
newsitem.headline: ICICI says loss provision not to hit net.

text.p: Leading finance firm Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) said on Wednesday losses if any from investments in shares would not impact its net profit for the year ended March 31, 1997.
Banking analysts said ICICI's portfolio investments -- which recorded a profit of 2,010 million in the fiscal ended March 31, 1996 - had incurred a notional loss of 2,660 million in the first half.
"If required we will make the necessary provisions but we will not write it out on our profit and loss account," said Kalpana Morparia, general manager at ICICI.
Morparia said the provision, if required, could be made against the firm's capital reserves which were close to four billion rupees.
Earlier in the day, analysts told Reuters current year profits could be impacted if these losses continued in the coming months.

K.V. Kamath, ICICI's managing director told analysts on Tuesday -- at a meeting to discuss first half results -- that he is likely to provide for any losses in the firm's accounts for the year ended March 31, 1997.
ICICI said on Tuesday net profit rose slightly to 2,663.0 million rupees in the six months to September 30, from 2,647.0 million a year ago. The results met most market expectations.
Analysts say ICICI's portfolio investments have underperformed Bombay's benchmark stocks index which fell around 3.8 percent during the six-month period.
They said the finance firm's portfolio comprised mainly second tier stocks which have seen a sharper fall.
